preflight.note: Opened from direct operator feedback after native Workbench validation: collection-heavy application pages require excessive vertical scrolling. The operator specifically requested Work tabs Proposed, Active, Deferred, Complete and the same user-centric low-scroll pattern across all primary pages. Clarified before implementation that RepoPact Workbench is cross-platform across Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS, so the IA must be adaptive rather than desktop-only.

acceptance_criteria.text: Introduce one reusable accessible cross-platform secondary-tab primitive used across primary application pages, with count support, clear selected state, correct tablist/tab/panel ARIA relationships, hardware-keyboard Left/Right/Home/End navigation, pointer/touch activation, focus-visible behavior, touch-friendly targets, and adaptive wrapping/compaction without page-wide horizontal scrolling.

Work presents exactly four primary lifecycle tabs in this order: Proposed, Active, Deferred, Complete; Active contains blocked records in a clearly labelled Blocked group before ordinary active/in-progress records while retaining each blocked record's canonical blocked status.

Work tab counts, selected-item behavior, search scoping, refresh/transition reconciliation, and useful default selection are deterministic; Active count includes active plus blocked, and a moved item cannot remain misleadingly selected under the wrong lifecycle tab.

Add reusable bounded client-side pagination for collection-heavy views with shared wide/compact page-size profiles, Previous/Next controls, disabled boundaries, start-end-of-total range text, deterministic ordering, touch-friendly controls, and safe reset/clamping after search/tab/snapshot/layout changes; Complete must not render the full completed corpus as one long page.

Dashboard uses concise Overview, Attention, and Session secondary views; Attention surfaces actionable validation/blocked-work signals with navigation rather than duplicating long source lists, and compact/mobile layouts prioritize actionable information without excessive ornamental vertical space.

Decisions uses Current, Proposed, Deferred, and History tabs with accepted -> Current, proposed -> Proposed, deferred -> Deferred, and rejected/superseded/deprecated -> History; counts and deterministic newest-first ordering use snapshot-derived typed metadata rather than N+1 detail reads.

Evidence uses Recent, Passed, Attention, and All tabs; Recent is newest-first and bounded, Passed contains passed runs, Attention contains failed/partial/blocked runs, All is paged, and summary rows surface useful result/time/work-item metadata without per-record detail fetches.

Graph uses Dependencies, Evidence, Governance, and All tabs derived from existing typed edge kinds; wide layouts retain the accessible table, while compact/mobile layouts provide an accessible stacked or equivalent representation that avoids page-wide horizontal scrolling and remains locally paged.

Validation uses Errors, Warnings, Info, and All tabs with counts and highest-severity non-empty default behavior, while preserving a compact all-clear state when no diagnostics exist and remaining readable at phone widths without horizontal page scrolling.
Analysis uses Constraints, Suggestions, and Facts tabs mapped exactly from the existing finding classification values and preserves remediation/explanatory content across wide and compact layouts.

Settings uses Appearance, Session, and Boundaries tabs; presentation/theme controls are discoverable under Appearance while session/watcher identity and native/security boundary explanations remain distinct, with compact/mobile headers avoiding redundant persistent controls where space is limited.

Any richer Decision/Evidence list metadata is exposed through typed Rust summary DTOs (or an equivalently typed snapshot projection), generated into TypeScript, and derived from the current cached RepositorySnapshot/index without opening every record, building fresh snapshots, or adding Git queries.

Secondary-tab, search, sort, page, breakpoint, and compact-detail presentation changes are operations over the cached native generation: executable tests prove they cause zero new repository snapshots, zero Git subprocesses, and no N+1 native detail calls for unchanged data.

Existing Work detail inspection, Decision/Evidence detail access, Rust-owned create/edit/transition mutation planning, stale-plan handling, watcher refresh, and repository-switch behavior remain intact and accessible after the information-architecture refactor.

Frontend and native-service tests cover tab mappings/counts, blocked-under-Active behavior, paging/search interaction, keyboard/ARIA semantics, touch activation, per-page sub-tab memory, repository-switch reset, Decisions/Evidence no-N+1 behavior, Graph/Validation/Analysis grouping, compact navigation, list-detail Back restoration, and WI057 process/cache non-regression.

The primary application shell is adaptive across Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS: wide layouts may use a persistent sidebar and split panes, while compact layouts collapse primary navigation into a drawer/sheet or equivalent, avoid an overloaded eight-item bottom bar, and preserve the same page/tab semantics without user-agent-dependent forks.

Compact/mobile Work, Decision, and Evidence flows use list-to-detail drill-in navigation with an explicit Back affordance and native/system Back integration where available; returning preserves selected secondary tab, query, pager/list context, orientation changes do not discard session state, essential actions do not depend on hover/right-click, safe-area and virtual-keyboard behavior are usable, and no nested tiny scroll regions are introduced.

Closeout verifies the requested low-scroll IA and wide/compact behavior natively on the available Windows host, records Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS build/runtime status separately and truthfully according to available hosts/toolchains/devices/simulators, preserves cross-platform Tauri security/capability boundaries, and records all relevant regression counts plus WI056 compatibility status without claiming unexecuted platforms as validated.
